messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In lions, one of the most striking dominant traits is the development of the mane in adult males. The presence and size of the mane is largely governed by the expression of genes involved in hair follicle growth and androgen sensitivity—particularly those linked to the androgen receptor pathway. In simple Mendelian terms, the allele that promotes robust mane growth behaves as a dominant factor in males, while females do not develop a mane because they lack the high circulating testosterone levels required to activate the same genetic program.
